Left the tab open on your MacBook Chrome at `app.lobu.ai/buremba/activity?lens=attention` so you can look at the approval queue directly. No code changed this session — this was read-only inspection (prod DB via MCP + DOM reads through the paired Chrome connection 479).

## What's healthy

**Data volume looks right.** 334k events, 11.7k entities, 25 live connections, 121 feeds. The Memory page counts reconcile exactly with the DB once you account for soft-deletes — Person 4,564 live / 11,348 rows, Task 164/175, Trip 39/47. Nothing is being miscounted.

**Approval flow renders correctly.** Ran the pending one end to end: `/buremba/activity?run_ids=871539` shows "Which meal do you like?" → Requested by Claude Code (lobu) → `Meal*` select with the 5 enum values → Confirm / Reject. The schema-driven input renders from `interaction_input_schema`. The two E2E asks from yesterday both completed with answers stored (`{"play":"Exec sponsor call"}`, `{}`). Approval history overall: 26 completed, 21 rejected/expired, 5 failed, 4 pending.

**Behaviors are actually running.** Social interest radar fires hourly at :25 and last completed 23:25 today. Hourly Task Collaborator completed at 19:00. Voice profile synthesis ran twice yesterday. Recent run mix over the last 3 days: 45 actions completed, 40 syncs completed, 1 behavior, 8 action failures (all Chrome tab-id/stale-ref noise from your own driving, not systemic).

**Ingestion is live** on chrome-history, x, linkedin, chrome-bookmarks — all within the last 2 hours.

## What doesn't look good

**1. The Behaviors page "last run" is wrong on all four cards.** This is the clearest bug.

| Card says | Actual last run |
|---|---|
| Hourly Task Collaborator — "Ran 19 days ago" | 2026-08-06 19:00 (4.5h ago) |
| Social interest radar — "Ran 1 day ago" | 2026-08-06 23:25 (~10 min ago) |
| Voice profile synthesis — "Next run in 3 days" (no last-run at all) | 2026-08-05 21:42 |
| Duplicate entity resolution — **"Never run"** | 2026-07-30 03:16, completed |

The sidebar RECENT list on the same page shows the correct times ("Social interest radar · 6 minutes ago"), so the card is reading a different, stale source than the sidebar. "Never run" on a behavior with completed runs is the giveaway.

**2. Dead approval cards in Needs attention.** The lens shows 5 "Action `observe` / `hotkey` / `type_text` needs approval — Review & approve" cards from 2–3 days ago. 12 notifications carry `approval_status: "pending"`, but only 4 have a live pending approval event (the meal ask + 2 LinkedIn prepare_comment + 1 X prepare_reply). The other 8 point at `approval_run_id`s that `operations.listRuns` can't surface at all — connection 447 has zero runs before Aug 5. Those buttons can't do anything. Compounding it: computer-use is now on `approval: auto`, so nothing will ever resolve them.

**3. The "31" badge is mostly not approvals.** 5 real approval cards + 26 unread Social-interest-radar digests. The count reads as urgent work when it's mostly a newsletter.

**4. The sidebar is where your "beautifully" claim breaks.** RECENT is 8 conversations titled "Reply with exactly: OK" and 2 titled "Reply with exactly the word: pong" — provider probe threads from yesterday, crowding out everything real. Below them, 5 entries titled `REDACTED` with "669 calls · Run SDK". That's a raw client id as a display name.

**5. Connector rot.** Google Calendar has been failing since Jul 29 with a 403 `ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT` — needs re-consent, 5 consecutive failures. Revolut is at 16 consecutive failures across 6 transaction feeds, all "session needs sign-in". WhatsApp messages feed has 12 consecutive `worker_claim_timeout`. 42 feeds are in failing state, though ~30 of those are the paused LinkedIn/Instagram takeout feeds missing `takeout_dir`, which is expected. The Connectors page also lists three zombie runtimes: "Chrome · 0 connectors · offline", "Device · Unknown platform · 0 connectors · offline", "Burak's MacBook Pro · macOS · 5 connectors · offline".

**6. Two smaller things.** All 8 `voice-profile` entities are soft-deleted, and the type doesn't appear on the Memory page — yet the Voice profile synthesis behavior is active and ran yesterday, so it's writing records that get deleted. Same for `topic`: 13 rows, all 13 deleted. Also `client.behaviors.list()` returns `{name, status}` with no `id`, so you can't chain it into `operations.listRuns({behavior_ids})` without a second lookup — I had to go to SQL.

## Confidence

- **Behaviors "last run" bug — 95.** Verified four-for-four against `operations.listRuns` per behavior id, and the sidebar on the same page disagrees with the card. Haven't read the frontend code to name the wrong field.
- **Dead approval cards — 85.** Confirmed the notification rows say pending and the events/runs behind them don't exist. Didn't click "Review & approve" to see the failure mode, so I can't tell you whether it errors or silently no-ops.
- **Data reconciliation and connector health — 90.** Direct DB counts and `feeds.list({health:'failing'})`, both live prod.
- **UI rendering — 85.** DOM text reads, no screenshots, so I can't speak to visual layout or styling.

## Next

1. Trace the Behaviors card's "Ran X ago" field in `packages/owletto` — the sidebar reads the right thing, so it's likely a stale `last_run_at` column vs. the runs table. That's a one-file fix with a clear reproducer.
2. Decide what to do with the 8 orphaned pending notifications — either reconcile them to `expired` on read, or backfill once. They'll sit in the badge forever otherwise.
3. Re-consent Google Calendar (needs the wider scope) and re-auth Revolut in the paired Chrome — both are one-time human actions I can't do for you.
4. Worth deciding whether provider-probe conversations should be excluded from sidebar RECENT, or whether the probe scripts should stop creating named threads. The sidebar is the first thing anyone sees in this org.

Found the actual root causes. Both are precise, and neither is what I'd have guessed from the symptoms.

## Why the Behaviors page lies

There are two different fields for "last run" and the two pages read different ones.

`packages/server/src/gateway/services/agent-thread-list.ts:283` — the **sidebar** — reads `last_run_completed_at`, a stamp written by a trigger on `runs`. Correct times.

`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_behaviors/list.ts:57` — the **Behaviors page** — selects `i.last_fired_at` and never selects `last_run_completed_at` at all. `behaviors-page.tsx:196` renders that into `LastRunChip`, which falls through to `"Never run"` when it's null (`behaviors-page.tsx:97`).

The DB confirms it exactly:

| Behavior | `last_fired_at` (what the card shows) | `last_run_completed_at` (truth) |
|---|---|---|
| Hourly Task Collaborator | 2026-07-19 → "Ran 19 days ago" | 2026-08-06 19:00 |
| Social interest radar | 2026-08-05 13:58 → "Ran 1 day ago" | 2026-08-06 23:25 |
| Voice profile synthesis | NULL → no chip | 2026-08-05 21:42 |
| Duplicate entity resolution | NULL → "Never run" | 2026-07-30 03:17 |

Four for four. `last_fired_at` only gets stamped on event-trigger activations, so any schedule-only behavior reads as never run. And `table-schema.ts:494` already documents `last_run_completed_at` as "what the listing orders by" — so the list is *sorted* by the right field and *labelled* with the wrong one.

## Why they generate nothing

**Voice profile synthesis is filtering on a handle that doesn't exist.** `examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts:1041`:

```
(connector_key = 'x' AND origin_type IN ('tweet','reply')
 AND lower(coalesce(metadata->>'author_handle','')) = 'buremba')
```

Your handle in the data is **`bu7emba`**. I checked: `bu7emba` has 24 tweets in the last 21 days (latest Aug 6 17:01); `buremba` has zero rows, ever. So `authored_recent` returns empty every run. Its other two arms are `twitter.takeout` and `linkedin.takeout` — both paused connections. The behavior has been synthesizing a voice profile from an empty set, which is why the Aug 5 run deleted all 4 existing profiles and wrote back exactly one (`X · taste`, run 863144). The org now has **zero live voice-profile entities**. And behavior 71 consumes `voice_profile` events as a context source, so the radar's tone matching is running on nothing too.

**Hourly Task Collaborator runs against dead inputs.** Its `recent_signals` source pulls `semantic_type IN ('message','thread','reminder','calendar_event','note')`. git push -q -u origin feat/voice-profile-handle 2>&1 | tail -3; gh pr create --title "fix(personal-agent): correct X author handle in voice-profile source" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

The `voice-profile-synthesis` Behavior's `authored_recent` source filters X posts on `metadata->>'author_handle' = 'buremba'`. The real handle is **`bu7emba`**, so the X arm of that source matched zero rows on every run since it was written.

Found while auditing why the `buremba` org's Behaviors run on schedule but produce nothing durable.

## Red → green

Same query, same 21-day window, prod `buremba` org — only the handle literal differs.

**Red** (`= 'buremba'`):
```
 rows_returned
---------------
             0
```

**Green** (`= 'bu7emba'`):
```
 rows_returned
---------------
            12
```

Corroborating: `SELECT lower(metadata->>'author_handle'), origin_type, count(*) FROM events WHERE connector_key IN ('x','twitter.takeout') AND lower(metadata->>'author_handle') IN ('buremba','bu7emba') GROUP BY 1,2` returns `bu7emba/tweet 24` and `bu7emba/bookmark 1`. `buremba` has never appeared as an author_handle.

The source's other two arms are `twitter.takeout` and `linkedin.takeout`, both on paused connections, so the whole source was returning empty — the Behavior has been synthesizing a voice profile from nothing.

## Scope

One line. `grep` over `origin/main` for `author_handle` confirms this is the only hardcoded handle literal in the repo; `examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts:172` is an alias-based eventSet mapping and is correct as written.

## Note for the reviewer

`examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts` has drifted from the live Behavior in the `buremba` org, independently of this change. Live version 6 declares `outputs.profiles` as an **event** output (`{ key: ["channel","mode"], event: "voice_profile" }`) and reads `existing_profiles` from `events WHERE semantic_type = 'voice_profile'`; this config still declares an **entity** output and reads from `entities`. Running `lobu apply` from this file would revert that migration. I did not touch it here — flagging so nobody applies this config assuming it is current.

## Gates

`make pre-pr` clean (typecheck, knip, biome, exposed-surface naming, gateway-llm gate).
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

## REGRESSED, then re-fixed 2026-08-06 — the repo config is the regression vector

The 2026-08-02 fix above **did not hold.** On 2026-08-06 I found Behavior 70 back on
`= 'buremba'`. Current prod version 6 (`version_id` 268) carried the dead handle again
and had **dropped the `authored_archive` source** that v3 (254) added — back to the same
3-source shape as the repo file.

`examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts:1041` on `origin/main` still contained
`= 'buremba'`. That file is the only place in the repo carrying the dead handle, and it
carries exactly the 3-source shape v6 has. **A hand-authored v6 copied its source SQL
from the stale repo config instead of from v3.** So the DB-only fix was always going to
be clobbered — fixing prod without fixing the config just resets the clock.

- Repo fix: **PR #2568** (`fix(personal-agent): correct X author handle in voice-profile source`).
  Red 0 rows / green 12 rows on the live 21-day query.
- Prod: created **version 7** (`version_id` 276) via `behaviors.createVersion`, changing
  ONLY `authored_recent`. Did NOT `lobu apply` — see drift note below.

**Lesson: a Behavior fix made only in the DB is not durable. Fix the config in the same
pass, or the next version author copies the bug forward.** Same class as
[[feedback_stale_tree_commit_reverts_merged_work]].

### Still missing after the re-fix

I restored the handle but **not `authored_archive`**. `authored_recent` still has the
21-day window, so the 1786-row / 15-year takeout corpus described above is still excluded.
Voice profiles are being built from ~12 recent posts. Re-adding that source is the next
step if the profiles read thin.

### The repo config has drifted from prod in TWO other ways — do not `lobu apply` it

Verified 2026-08-06 against `behavior_versions` 268:

| | repo `lobu.config.ts` | live prod v6 |
|---|---|---|
| `outputs.profiles` | `{ entity: voiceProfile }` | `{ event: "voice_profile" }` |
| `existing_profiles` | reads `entities WHERE entity_type='voice-profile'` | reads `events WHERE semantic_type='voice_profile'` |

Prod was deliberately migrated entity→event output. `lobu apply` from this repo would
revert that migration. This is why I used `createVersion` instead.

## Why the org still shows ZERO voice profiles (separate cause, already fixed)

Run 861521 (2026-08-05 19:06 UTC, weekly window Aug 3–9, `content_analyzed: 13`) failed:

> Failed to save voice profiles due to persistent `events_client_id_fkey` foreign key
> constraint and timeout errors.

`events.client_id` FKs to `oauth_clients`; worker direct-auth sets the synthetic
`clientId: 'lobu-worker'`, which has no row. Fixed by **#2534** (`695c8f302`, merged
2026-08-05 22:03 BST) — i.e. ~2h AFTER this run failed. Confirmed deployed:
`git merge-base --is-ancestor 695c8f302 bb2dcba04` passes against the live
`/api/health` revision. Regression test:
`packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/events/worker-save-content-fk.test.ts`.

**That failure consumed the Aug 3–9 weekly window.** `computePendingWindow`
(`packages/server/src/utils/window-utils.ts:112`) chains off the last window's
`window_start` and clamps to the current period, so a manual `behaviors.trigger` resolves
to the SAME already-completed window and short-circuits — my trigger (run 872975)
completed in ~20s having written no window row and no events. **The behavior cannot
re-run until the next Monday period (2026-08-10 06:40).** Verify the profiles then; if
they are still absent the cause is NOT the handle.

Related: [[reference_x_ignores_intent_text_param]].

content.text:
Review is still running. Here's where things stand — and the story changed materially from my first report.

## The handle bug had already been fixed once, and regressed

My own notes from Aug 2 record fixing exactly this: Behavior 70 was moved to version 3 (`version_id` 254) querying `bu7emba`, plus a new `authored_archive` source with no date filter to reach the 15-year, 1786-row takeout corpus.

Current prod version 6 was back on `= 'buremba'` **and** had dropped `authored_archive` — the same three-source shape as `examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts`, which still carried the dead handle on `origin/main`. Whoever authored v6 copied the source SQL from the stale config rather than from v3.

So the real lesson is that fixing a Behavior only in the DB doesn't hold. That's why the config fix matters more than the prod one:

- **PR #2568** — `examples/personal-agent/lobu.config.ts`, one line, `buremba` → `bu7emba`. `make pre-pr` clean.
- **Prod version 7** (`version_id` 276) via `createVersion`, changing only `authored_recent`. I deliberately did *not* `lobu apply`.

I didn't apply because the repo config has drifted from prod in two more ways: prod declares `outputs.profiles` as an **event** output where the config says **entity**, and prod's `existing_profiles` reads `events` where the config reads `entities`. Prod was deliberately migrated entity→event. Applying would revert that.

## Why the org has zero voice profiles — not the handle

Window `4824719`, run 861521, Aug 5 19:06 UTC, `content_analyzed: 13`:

> Failed to save voice profiles due to persistent `events_client_id_fkey` foreign key constraint and timeout errors.

The behavior analyzed 13 items, produced profiles, and couldn't persist them. `events.client_id` FKs to `oauth_clients`; worker auth sets a synthetic `clientId: 'lobu-worker'` with no row.

That's already fixed — **#2534** (`695c8f302`), merged Aug 5 22:03 BST, about two hours *after* this run failed. I confirmed it's live: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 695c8f302 bb2dcba04` passes against the deployed `/api/health` revision. There's a regression test at `packages/server/src/__tests__/integration/events/worker-save-content-fk.test.ts`.

## Why my re-run produced nothing

The failed run consumed the Aug 3–9 weekly window. `computePendingWindow` (`packages/server/src/utils/window-utils.ts:112`) chains off the last window's `window_start` and clamps to the current period, so `behaviors.trigger` resolves to the same already-completed window and short-circuits. Run 872975 finished in ~20s having written no window row and no events.

**Behavior 70 cannot re-run until Monday 2026-08-10 06:40.** I could not prove the fix end-to-end, and I'm not going to claim I did.

That same file documents the daily-granularity behavior I flagged earlier: there is no hourly granularity, so behavior 71's hourly cron necessarily shares one daily window, and the comment names behavior 71 spending a full day re-completing the previous day's window.

## Confidence

- **Handle is wrong, fix is correct — 95.** Red 0 rows / green 12 rows on the live query; `bu7emba` has 24 tweets, `buremba` has never appeared.
- **Regression via the stale config — 80.** The config is the only place in the repo with the dead handle and matches v6's shape exactly. I can't prove it directly: `behavior_versions` doesn't store `sources`, so historical source SQL isn't queryable. Resting partly on my Aug 2 notes.
- **FK bug caused the profile loss, and is fixed — 90.** Error text from the window row, fix commit ancestry checked against the deployed SHA.
- **Fix actually regenerates profiles — 0.** Untested. Window is closed until Aug 10.

## Where I stopped, and why

Two of the three things I proposed are still not done, and one is blocked on you:

1. **Behaviors-page last-run chip** — root-caused precisely (`manage_behaviors/list.ts:57` selects `last_fired_at`; `behaviors-page.tsx:196` renders it; `agent-thread-list.ts:283` uses the correct `last_run_completed_at`). The fix adds a field to the behaviors list API response, and AGENTS.md requires your sign-off before I change API surface. I asked earlier and didn't get an answer, so I held.
2. **Orphaned approval notifications** — not started.
3. **`authored_archive`** — I restored the handle but not the source that reaches the historical corpus, so profiles will still be built from ~12 recent posts. Re-adding it is probably what actually makes them good.

Next, if you want it: say the word on the API field and I'll do the Behaviors chip; and tell me whether to restore `authored_archive` and reconcile the repo config's entity→event drift, since that's a design call I shouldn't make for you. I'll report the review verdict on #2568 when it lands — I'm not merging it while you're away.

All gates run. #2568 is green on everything mine, blocked by something that isn't.

## PR #2568 status

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `make pre-pr` | clean (typecheck, knip, biome, exposed-surface, gateway-llm) |
| `make review` | pass — bug_free 88, simplicity 100, slop 0, **0 bugs, 0 blockers**, risk low |

| unit / migrations / format-lint / base-branch-guard | pass |

| **check-drift** | **fail — not caused by this PR** |

Note on the first review run: it died with `reviewer process exited with status 1` because the codex reviewer is still broken. Re-ran with `REVIEWER_CLI=claude`, which is what produced the verdict above. Also worth saying plainly — `make review 2>&1 | tail` exited 0 *both* times, including the failed one, because the exit code came from `tail`. I read the verdict marker rather than trusting the exit status.

## The thing blocking merge is repo-wide, not mine

```
Pinned (parent): 884859e9c2d9028bdaa1c1fb4c9cd3a13e0d5572
owletto/main:    3da851cf380e295b1ecff00f60e92fc8ca93eb3e

Commits needing a parent bump:
3da851cf fix(api): resolve URL org scope subdomain-first so first-class
         type URLs stop 404ing (#741)
```

owletto#741 was merged without the parent pointer bump, so `check-drift` fails on **every** open PR right now, not just this one. The guard's own message says to fix it as a separate PR.

I'm not doing that unilaterally. A pointer bump ships someone else's frontend change to prod and owes before/after visual proof through `make ui-review` — that's a real piece of work and a prod-visible decision, not a rubber stamp while you're away. Say the word and I'll do it properly.

## What's actually delivered vs. still owed

**Delivered:** the config fix is committed, reviewed clean, and sitting on #2568. Prod Behavior 70 is on version 7 with the corrected handle. `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` is one file, one line — I checked the file list matches exactly.

**Owed, and I want to be blunt about it:** you asked for these to work and generate things. I have not proven that. Behavior 70's weekly window is closed until **Monday 2026-08-10 06:40**, so the fix is unverified end-to-end. That's four days out — past anything I can schedule a wakeup for, so it needs a deliberate check then. If the profiles are still missing on Aug 11, the handle was not the cause and I was wrong.

**Not started:** the Behaviors-page chip (blocked on your call about adding `last_run_completed_at` to the list API), the orphaned approval notifications, and the `authored_archive` source — that last one is probably what makes the profiles genuinely good rather than merely non-empty, since without it they're built from ~12 recent posts instead of the 1786-row archive.

## Confidence

- **#2568 is correct and safe to merge — 92.** Red/green on the live query, independent review clean, one-line diff verified against `origin/main`.
- **It makes voice profiles regenerate — 0.** Cannot be tested until Aug 10. Unchanged from before.
- **check-drift is unrelated to my change — 95.** The failure names owletto#741 and the pinned SHA; my diff touches no submodule.

Three things I'd like from you when you're back: whether to add the API field so I can fix the Behaviors chip, whether to open the owletto pointer bump that unblocks the merge queue, and whether to restore `authored_archive` plus reconcile the config's entity→event drift — that last one is a design decision about how voice profiles are stored, which is yours to make, not mine.

It's your X handle — the account the `x` connector is syncing.

The connection itself is named for it: connection 399, slug `x-twitter-bu7emba`, display name **`X (@bu7emba)`**. And every event under that handle carries `author_name: "burak emre"` with URLs like `x.com/bu7emba/status/...`. A few of the recent ones:

- "my new non-frontier favorite model is deepseek v4 pro, used to be glm 5.2" (Aug 6)
- "after x changed its algorithm... it got me thinking about how it applies to what we're building at lobu" (Aug 4)
- "claude code got dumber when I moved my work to mac mini..." (Jul 24)

25 events total under that handle. `buremba` appears zero times as an `author_handle`, ever.

The confusion is understandable: `buremba` is your GitHub name and the stem for nearly every connection slug in the org — `gmail-buremba`, `linkedin-buremba`, `revolut-buremba`, and the org slug itself. So `buremba` is right everywhere *except* as an X handle, which is the one place the config used it. `x.com/buremba` isn't your account.

1	---

3	description: "A zsh function named `log` shadows /usr/bin/log and makes every `log show` return nothing — plus how Owletto's Mac app logging actually works (Log.swift, ~/Library/Logs/Owletto, LOBU_OWLETTO_LOG_DIR)"

9	---
10	
11	## The trap: `log` is shadowed in this shell
12	
13	There is a zsh function named `log` on this machine. Every `log show …` invocation
14	hits it, not `/usr/bin/log`, and it fails with:
15	
16	    (eval):log:1: too many arguments
17	
18	With `2>/dev/null` on the command — which is the natural thing to write — this
19	looks like **an empty result set**, not an error. It cost a wrong conclusion
20	("the Mac app emits no logs at all") that survived three separate predicates and
21	got as far as being reported to the user. There were 79,897 lines.
22	
23	**Always use `/usr/bin/log show`, and never suppress stderr on a diagnostic
24	command whose empty output you intend to reason from.** An absence you can't
25	distinguish from an error is not evidence — same family as
26	[[feedback_absence_needs_origin_main_grep]].
27	
28	Useful predicates once you're calling the real binary:
29	
30	    /usr/bin/log show --last 3h --predicate 'process == "Owletto"' --style compact
31	    /usr/bin/log show --last 3h --predicate 'subsystem == "ai.lobu.mac"' --info --debug
32	
33	## How the Mac app logs (as of owletto `feat/mac-perms-logging`)
34	
35	`apps/mac/Owletto/Log.swift` — `Log.info/.error/.debug(_ category:, _ message:)`.
36	Categories: `app`, `sync`, `worker`, `permissions`, `connector`, `runner`, `whatsapp`.
37	
38	- **os.Logger** under subsystem `ai.lobu.mac`. Interpolations are `privacy: .public`
39	  — the DEFAULT is `.private`, which renders every value as `<private>`; that alone
40	  makes a unified-log search look empty while the app is talking normally.
41	- **File** at `~/Library/Logs/Owletto/owletto.log`, rotating at 5 MB to `.log.1`.
42	  The file exists because Owletto is `LSUIElement` launched by LaunchServices, so
43	  `print()`/stdout goes nowhere. Reachable in-app via the "App log" button on the
44	  error detail (the older "See logs" only appeared for `serverMode == .local`).
45	- Writes go to a serial background queue. **Never make the logger touch the
46	  filesystem on the calling thread** — `AppState` is `@MainActor` and a blocking
47	  `open()` there is the exact bug in [[feedback_never_hot_swap_owletto_app_remotely]].
48	- `LOBU_OWLETTO_LOG_DIR` redirects the sink; that's how `Tests/LogDedupeTests.swift`
49	  runs without truncating the user's real log.
50	- **Only the app bundle writes to `~/Library/Logs/Owletto`** (owletto #664).
51	  `directoryURL` checks `Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier == "ai.lobu.mac"` and sends
52	  anything else to a per-pid temp dir. See the false-incident section below for
53	  why the env override was not sufficient on its own.
54	
55	## `appendingPathComponent` decides trailing slashes by STATTING the disk
56	
57	Comparing two `URL`s for the same directory is unsafe: `URL` equality treats a
58	trailing slash as significant, and `appendingPathComponent(_:)` **without** the
59	`isDirectory:` label determines whether to add one by hitting the filesystem. So
60	`URL(...).appendingPathComponent("Library/Logs/Owletto")` gains a slash only on a
61	machine where that directory already exists.
62	
63	That shipped a test green on this dev box (app installed → directory exists) that
64	would fail on a fresh CI runner, with **both sides printing the identical path**
65	in the failure message — maximally confusing. Caught by Codesmith in owletto #668.
66	
67	**Compare `.path` strings, and always pass `isDirectory:` explicitly.** Applies to
68	any filesystem URL assertion, not just logging.
69	
70	**Repeat suppression is keyed per distinct message, NOT per consecutive line.**
71	The first implementation collapsed only adjacent duplicates and did nothing at
72	all, because the poll loop emits several different errors per cycle so identical
73	lines interleave (`A B A B A`). It looked correct in review and was only caught
74	by reading the produced file back. Mutation-tested: restoring the consecutive-only
75	logic turns `LogDedupeTests` red.
76	
77	## Adding a Swift file to the Mac app
78	
79	`Owletto.xcodeproj` has ONE target and **no** file-system-synchronized groups, so
80	a new `.swift` file on disk is invisible to the build until it is registered in
81	four places in `project.pbxproj` (PBXBuildFile, PBXFileReference, the group's
82	children, the Sources phase) with hand-assigned hex IDs. Symptom is misleading:
83	only *some* files report `cannot find 'X' in scope` because the compiler bails
84	mid-batch, which reads as a target-membership problem.
85	
86	The standalone tests under `apps/mac/Tests/` compile production sources listed in
87	each file's **header comment**, which `run-tests.sh` executes verbatim. Adding a
88	new dependency to a production file therefore breaks every test that compiles it
89	until you add the new source to those headers too — three broke this way here.
90	Always run the whole suite (`apps/mac/Tests/run-tests.sh`), never just the new test.

`~/Library/Logs/Owletto/owletto.log` on **Burak's MacBook Pro**:


The app **is running** (`/Applications/Owletto.app/Contents/MacOS/Owletto`, pid 1220) —

Everything pinned to worker `2c295bed` stopped. Last successful WhatsApp execution
`2026-08-06T01:12:34Z` matches `wa-local-buremba`'s last event ingest **exactly** — that
timestamp pair is the cheapest confirmation that the worker, not the connector, is the cause.

Symptom at the feed layer is `worker_claim_timeout` (feed 309, 12 consecutive failures).
**`worker_claim_timeout` means "no worker claimed the job", i.e. the DEVICE is gone — it is
not a connector bug.** Do not debug the connector.

Downstream: Behavior 5 (Hourly Task Collaborator) starved, because its `recent_signals`
source needs `semantic_type IN ('message','thread','reminder','calendar_event','note')` and

content.text:
Worked through all four. Here's where each one stands.

## Behaviors, one by one

**Hourly Task Collaborator (5) — now generating.** It was running hourly against dead inputs. I revived its sources, triggered it, and it produced three real tasks at 23:58:09:
- "Register for the 'Coding in Flow: From Autocomplete to Agentic IDE' event" — from a Gmail thread
- "Buy peanut butter", "Buy yoghurt" — from Reminders

Its `recent_signals` source went from **0 rows to 80**.

**Social interest radar (71) — already working; I was wrong to imply otherwise.** It's emitting 2–7 signal events every hour without a gap. The `content_analyzed: 0` I flagged earlier is a bookkeeping artifact on the daily window row, not a functional failure. Nothing to fix.

**Duplicate entity resolution (20) — was two weeks behind.** It processes one weekly window per run and was stuck at Jul 19–26. Three triggers walked it forward to the current week (Aug 3–10). It now analyzes correctly — "Found 4 groups of potentially duplicate person profiles based on shared name_key" — but **emits nothing actionable**: the reaction calls `resolve_duplicates` and no merge gets queued, because no deterministic identity rule proves them. That matches the historical pattern where its approvals all expired with "No configured deterministic identity rule proves this merge." It runs, it thinks, it can't act. Fixing that means configuring identity rules, which is a design decision I'm leaving to you.

**Voice profile synthesis (70) — fixed but unproven.** Handle corrected in PR #2568 and prod version 7. Still blocked until **Monday Aug 10 06:40**: its weekly window Aug 3–9 was consumed by the run that died on the FK bug, and `computePendingWindow` clamps to the current period, so retriggering resolves to the same spent window. Behavior 20 could catch up because it was *behind*; 70 is *current*, so there's nothing to advance into.

## Data collection

Three feeds had **no cron at all** — manual-only, which is why they silently went stale. Triggered them, and they pulled real data:

| Feed | Was | New events |
|---|---|---|
| Gmail threads | stale since Jul 29 | 40 |
| Spotify recently_played | stale since Jul 29 | 50 |
| Reminders | stale since Jul 31 | 8 |

Then gave all four (plus YouTube) staggered crons so they stay fresh: `12 */2`, `22 */2`, `32 */3`, `42 8`. Active scheduled feeds went 9 → 13, and every one is succeeding except WhatsApp.

## The Mac situation — it's the MacBook, not the Mac mini

The Mac mini is fine. **Both** its workers are online and doing real work — X, LinkedIn, Revolut-Chrome, computer-use, mac-shell, Reminders.

The dead one is **this MacBook Pro's native worker**. From `~/Library/Logs/Owletto/owletto.log`:

```
2026-08-06T01:25:24Z [ERROR] [sync] ... (401) {"error":"invalid_token",
    "error_description":"Invalid or expired access token"}
2026-08-06T01:25:29Z [ERROR] [sync] credentials invalid, dropping back to connection card
```

The app **is running** (pid 1220) — it relaunched at 02:12 and hit the same 401 immediately, then went silent for 21 hours. A signed-out worker stops polling entirely. Last successful WhatsApp execution was `01:12:34`, which matches that connector's last ingested event to the second.

That single sign-out is what's holding down WhatsApp, Apple Calendar, Screen Time, Photos, and Local Folder. **You need to re-authenticate in the Owletto app's connection card** — I won't touch credentials.

Also worth knowing: the connection slugs lie about which machine they are. `chrome-macbook` is the **Mac mini**; `chrome-buremba` is the MacBook.

## One thing I ran into

Prod went to **zero pods** mid-session and served 503s on every request. It was a Flux HelmRelease upgrade doing a zero-overlap cutover — old ReplicaSet scaled to 0 before the new one was ready. It recovered in ~10s on revision `b0198396`. Not caused by anything I did, and self-healed, but that's a real hard-503 window on every deploy, and the same 503s appear in the Owletto Mac log from earlier days.

## Confidence

- **Behavior 5 generating — 95.** Three task entities with a creation timestamp matching the run's completion exactly.
- **Feeds revived and scheduled — 95.** Counted new events by connection, then re-read the feed list to confirm crons stuck.
- **MacBook worker is the cause — 90.** Log 401, plus the last-execution/last-ingest timestamp match.
- **Behavior 20 caught up — 85.** Window rows advanced to Aug 3–10. That it produces nothing actionable is observed, not yet root-caused to a specific line.
- **Behavior 70 — 0 on output.** Unchanged; can't test until Aug 10.

## Next

1. Re-auth Owletto on this MacBook — that's the single highest-value action left and only you can do it. WhatsApp and Calendar come back the moment you do, and Behavior 5 gets much richer input.
2. Google Calendar needs re-consent for the wider scope; Revolut needs a sign-in in the paired Chrome.
3. Connection 375 has **six duplicate `transactions` feeds** (331, 369–373), all failing. Looks like accumulated clutter worth pruning — but that's a delete, so I'd want your nod.
4. Check the voice profiles after Monday. If they're still empty then, the handle wasn't the cause and I'll dig again.

content.text:
Yes — you were right, and there's a real bug. Two, actually.

## The app is authed. It's authed to the wrong org.

The Owletto Mac app doesn't own its identity. On a 401 it calls `refreshSession()`, which **shells out to the `lobu` CLI** (`AppState.swift:2422` → `lobu whoami --json`). So the app's identity is whatever your **global CLI context** happens to be.

Your active context was `v146` — a leftover worktree context:

```
$ lobu whoami --json                                    # before
{"loggedIn":true,"context":"v146","orgSlug":"lobu-team", ...}
```

`loggedIn: true`. Valid token. **Wrong organization.** The MacBook's device worker and its five connections (WhatsApp, Apple Calendar, Screen Time, Photos, Local Folder) live in `buremba`. The server correctly 401s a `lobu-team` token asking for `buremba` worker jobs.

I switched it back:

```
$ lobu context use prod
$ lobu whoami --json                                    # after
{"loggedIn":true,"context":"prod","orgSlug":"buremba",
 "email":"emrekabakci@gmail.com", ...}
```

`~/.config/lobu/credentials.json` makes the distinction obvious in hindsight: `prod` carries `email`, `userId`, and a **refreshToken**; `v146` (and `dbg`, `lease2`, `ctx-*`) carry only a bare 40-char PAT. Those are e2e/worktree throwaways.

And here's the kicker — **`make task-setup CONTEXT=1` registers a CLI context.** Per AGENTS.md that's the standard way to spin up a worktree. So creating a worktree can silently sign your production Mac worker out of the right org, with no error anywhere.

## Bug 1: the Mac app has no org affinity

It inherits an ambient global CLI context and never checks that the context's org matches the device worker's org. A dev-loop side effect takes down production data collection.

## Bug 2: a wrong-org 401 is misclassified as "session revoked"

`AppState.swift:1590`:

```swift
} catch SyncDispatcher.CycleError.credentialsInvalid {
    Log.error(.sync, "credentials invalid, dropping back to connection card")
    stopAutoPoll()
    credentials = nil
    ...
    sessionExpired = true
```

Terminal. No backoff, no retry. A recoverable condition — wrong context, fixable in one command — becomes a permanent stop requiring manual UI re-auth. That's **23 hours of lost collection** from WhatsApp, Calendar, Screen Time, Photos and Local Folder, and it's why Behavior 5 was starving.

The retry logic *upstream* of that is careful (401 → refresh → retry once → only then give up). The gap is that it re-asks the same wrong source and treats a second identical rejection as proof of revocation.

## Where I was wrong

My earlier "just re-authenticate in the app" was the wrong call. I read the 401 in the log and stopped at the first plausible cause instead of asking why a running, authed app would produce one. The keychain credential was there the whole time. Thanks for pushing back.

## Confidence

- **Root cause — 92.** `whoami` showed `orgSlug: lobu-team` before and `buremba` after; the code path from 401 → CLI → `credentialsInvalid` is read directly from source.
- **Recovery without touching the app — unknown.** `stopAutoPoll()` is terminal, so the app most likely still needs one click on the reconnect prompt in the menubar even though the CLI session is now healthy. I have a check running and will confirm.

I did not restart or touch the app — that's a line I won't cross remotely.

## Next

1. If the check shows it hasn't resumed, click the reconnect prompt in the Owletto menubar once. The CLI session underneath is already correct, so it should not need a full sign-in.
2. Worth filing both bugs — the org-affinity one especially, since it'll recur every time you use `CONTEXT=1`.
3. Habit worth forming: `lobu whoami --json | grep orgSlug` before blaming a device worker.

Confirmed, and it refines what I told you. The check shows the log never advanced — same last line, same mtime.

## What the app was actually using

That log line I'd skimmed past has the answer:

```
2026-08-06T02:12:33.534Z [INFO] [worker] capabilities=[...] context=lobu
```

At launch it was on context **`lobu`** — not `v146`. And here's what the three contexts actually hold:

| context | identity | refreshToken |
|---|---|---|
| `lobu` | `install@buraks-macbook-pro.local` | **no** |
| `v146` | *(none — bare 40-char PAT)* | **no** |
| `prod` | `emrekabakci@gmail.com` | **yes** |

Context `lobu` points at `https://app.lobu.ai` but holds a **local-install credential** — a `user_install_*` identity minted for a local server. Against prod that's a guaranteed 401. `v146` was simply what had become active by the time I sampled it.

So my "wrong org" framing was directionally right but not precise. The accurate statement: **the app follows the ambient global CLI context, and none of the contexts it landed on held a valid prod session for `buremba`.** Only `prod` does, and that's now the active one:

```

orgSlug = buremba, email = emrekabakci@gmail.com
```

## It will not self-heal — two independent reasons

1. `stopAutoPoll()` on `credentialsInvalid` is terminal. No backoff, no retry.
2. `currentContextName` is only refreshed "on launch, on account-row expansion, and after any local edit (switchContext / addContext)" (`AppState.swift:124-130`). A context change made externally by the CLI is invisible to a running app.

Both are confirmed by the log: unchanged through the whole check.

- **Quit and relaunch Owletto.** On launch it re-reads `currentContext`, which is now `prod`. Simplest.
- Or open the menubar, expand the account row (that re-reads contexts), and hit reconnect.

It should not need a full sign-in — the underlying `prod` session has a live refresh token and I confirmed it refreshes cleanly.

I'm not restarting it for you; that's the line I won't cross remotely.

The app resolves auth from an ambient global CLI context with **no check that the context's URL, credential type, and org actually match the device worker it's polling for**. A context named `lobu` holding a local-install credential aimed at production is silently accepted, produces a 401, and is then classified as "session revoked" — permanently stopping collection with nothing surfaced in the UI. That's how 23 hours of WhatsApp, Calendar, Screen Time, Photos and Local Folder data went missing while the app looked fine.

Two concrete guards worth having: validate that the resolved context is a real remote session before polling prod, and make `credentialsInvalid` retry with backoff rather than latch.

A local-install credential against prod = guaranteed 401. The app classified that as "session revoked" and stopped polling for 23 HOURS. Nothing surfaced it — the menubar looked fine. Five connections (whatsapp.local, apple.calendar, apple.screen_time, apple.photos, local.directory, all on device worker `2c295bed-1dfa-4c8b-9f58-c20a62aadfc2` in org `buremba`) silently stopped collecting, which starved Behavior 5.

Note `~/.config/lobu/credentials.json` distinguishes real vs throwaway contexts: real ones (`prod`) carry `email` + `userId` + `refreshToken`; throwaway e2e/worktree ones (`lobu`, `v146`, `dbg`, `lease2`, `ctx-*`) carry only a bare accessToken.

Aggravating factor: `make task-setup NAME=<x> CONTEXT=1` REGISTERS AND SWITCHES a CLI context. So routine worktree creation can silently sign the production Mac worker out.

## What to build

Two guards. Judge the exact shape yourself after reading the code — this is the intent, not a spec to follow blindly:

1. **Context/identity validation before polling.** The app must not silently poll prod with a credential that cannot possibly work. At minimum detect the mismatch (local-install credential aimed at a remote URL; context org != the device worker's org) and surface it as a distinct, actionable state — NOT as "session revoked".
2. **`credentialsInvalid` must stop latching.** A recoverable condition (wrong/stale context) currently requires manual UI re-auth. Make it retry with backoff, and/or re-read `currentContext` so an external `lobu context use prod` heals it. Fail-closed on genuinely revoked sessions is still correct — do not make it retry a truly dead session forever.

Do NOT paper over this by just re-authing or by widening what counts as a valid token.

## Hard constraints

- CRITICAL: the CLI context is currently `prod` and MUST stay that way — the user's production Mac worker depends on it. Do NOT run `make task-setup ... CONTEXT=1`. If anything switches it, restore with `lobu context use prod` and verify `lobu whoami --json` reports `"orgSlug":"buremba"`.
- Swift tests: `apps/mac/Tests/run-tests.sh` — run the WHOLE suite, not just your new test. Adding a dependency to a production file breaks every test whose header comment compiles it (see reference in AGENTS.md/GOTCHAS).
- Adding a new .swift file requires registering it in FOUR places in `project.pbxproj`. Prefer editing existing files.
- Do not suppress stderr on diagnostic commands. `log` is shadowed by a zsh function on this box — use `/usr/bin/log`, or just read `~/Library/Logs/Owletto/owletto.log` (more reliable).
- Red→green evidence is mandatory; paste both outputs into the PR body.

## E2E verification (the user explicitly asked for this — a green typecheck is NOT acceptable)

You are running ON the affected machine (Burak's MacBook Pro), so you can test for real:
1. RED: with the fix absent, `client.feeds.trigger({feed_id: 309})` (whatsapp.local) ends `worker_claim_timeout` after ~135s. That is the live reproducer. Use the lobu MCP tools (run_sdk/query_sdk/query_sql) — they are bound to org buremba.

## Shipping

Owletto is a submodule. Push owletto FIRST so the SHA is reachable, THEN bump the parent pointer:
  git -C <worktree>/packages/owletto push -u origin feat/mac-context-auth
  git -C <worktree> add packages/owletto && git -C <worktree> commit && push

# Testing Behaviors end to end

I learned most of this the hard way in the last hour, so here's what actually works and where it breaks.

## The recipe that works today

**Step 0 — assert the source returns rows, before running anything.** Take the Behavior's `sources[].query` verbatim and run it through `query_sql`. This is the highest-yield check and it's free. The `bu7emba` bug was 0 rows vs 12 on the same query. Most "the Behavior does nothing" cases are starvation, not logic.

**Step 1 — read the window state, or your trigger is meaningless.**

```sql
SELECT id, granularity, window_start, window_end, run_id, content_analyzed
FROM canvas_windows WHERE watcher_id = <id> ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 3
```

`computePendingWindow` (`packages/server/src/utils/window-utils.ts`) chains off the last window's `window_start` and clamps to the current period. Three consequences that will fool you:

- **Behind** → each trigger advances exactly one period. Behavior 20 needed three triggers to walk from Jul 19 to the current week.
- **Current and already consumed** → the trigger silently no-ops. Behavior 70 returned `status: completed`, `error: null`, in ~20s, having written no window and no events.
- **Hourly cron → DAILY window.** There is no hourly granularity, so every run in a day shares one window.

**Step 2 — trigger, then poll to a terminal status.** `behaviors.trigger({behavior_id})` → `operations.getRun`.

**Step 3 — assert on output, never on status.** This is the one that matters. `completed` proved nothing twice today.

| Output kind | Where to assert |
|---|---|
| entity outputs | new `entities` rows stamped at the run's `completed_at` |
| event outputs | `events WHERE run_id = <id>` or `metadata->>'behavior_id'` |
| window | `canvas_windows.content_analyzed > 0` + populated `extracted_data` |
| reaction effects | `notifications.list`, `operations.listRuns` |

Don't trust the window row alone: Behavior 5 wrote three real task entities while its `canvas_windows` row still read `content_analyzed: 0, {"tasks": []}`.

**Step 4 — the real error hides in the window, not the run.** Run 861521 had `error_message: null` at run level. The actual failure was at `canvas_windows.extracted_data->'run_metadata'->>'error'`: *"Failed to save voice profiles due to persistent events_client_id_fkey..."*. Always check that path before concluding a run was clean.

## What you can't do today, and it's the important part

**There is no dry run for Behaviors.** Session `dryRun` is a dead flag — zero read sites in the repo. So every e2e Behavior test executes **real side effects**: real Slack posts via `conversations/send`, real connector actions, real notifications. That's why I triggered 5, 20 and 70 but deliberately did not go looking for more to run.

**You can't replay a past window or force a fresh one.** Behavior 70's fix is unverifiable until Monday for exactly this reason. That's a structural gap, not my impatience.

## The thing that fixes it is already in flight

Umbrella issue **#2564**. PR 1 (`runs.outcome`) is merged as **#2566** — and its squash commit `b0198396` is precisely the revision that deployed mid-session tonight and caused the 503s I watched. It classifies every terminal run `infra_error` / `agent_error` / `scoreable`, which is the prerequisite for any honest pass/fail signal. It's prod-verified and backfilled: 13,454 rows, and the headline is that **91% of all Behavior failures in history were infra, not the agent**.

PR 2 is capture mode — the server forcing `dryRun` from the run type rather than the agent opting in. The per-method machinery already exists (`sandbox/method-metadata.ts` classifies 131 SDK methods; `run-script.ts` already implements true capture with `sideEffectPreview`); the only gap is activation. Worktree `eval-capture-mode` is already created. **That PR is what turns "test a Behavior end to end" from a real-side-effects gamble into something you can run repeatedly.**

One number worth internalizing while designing any of this: there are only **389 scoreable Behavior runs in all of prod history**. That's the entire dataset. Don't design for thousands.

## Confidence

- **The recipe — 90.** Every step is something I executed against prod tonight, including the failure modes.
- **Window mechanics — 85.** Read from `window-utils.ts` and corroborated by three Behaviors behaving exactly as it predicts. I have not read the dispatch path that decides whether to create a window at all, which is why Behavior 70's no-op is described rather than fully explained.
- **No dry run — 90.** From the spike recorded against #2564, not re-verified by me tonight.

## Next

1. I can write the Step 0–4 recipe up as a reusable harness — one script that takes a `behavior_id`, checks sources, snapshots window state, triggers, and diffs outputs. That's a genuinely reusable thing and doesn't need capture mode.
2. PR 2 (capture mode) is the unblock for repeatable testing; the worktree exists if you want it picked up.
3. Behavior 70 still owes its Monday check.
4. #2568 is still green-but-blocked on the owletto drift — the teammate's pointer bump may clear it, and I'll confirm when it reports.

# Plan — make the `buremba` Behaviors actually produce, and make failure visible

## Context

This started as "check buremba org, is everything building beautifully". It isn't, and the
interesting part is *why it looked fine*. Every Behavior reported `status: completed`. Runs
fired on schedule. The menubar said connected. Nothing was broken in a way anything surfaced —
and meanwhile four Behaviors between them produced almost nothing for days.

The causes turned out to be independent, which is why no single fix helps:

| # | Cause | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | X handle filter was `buremba`; real handle is `bu7emba` | source query: 0 rows vs 12. **Regressed** — fixed 2026-08-02, reintroduced from the stale repo config |
| 2 | `events_client_id_fkey` ate a run's output | window 4824719 `run_metadata.error`; fixed by #2534, deployed |
| 3 | MacBook's Owletto worker sent a loopback-only device PAT to prod | `owletto.log` 401 → `stopAutoPoll()`, silent 22h outage, 5 connectors dead |
| 4 | Three feeds had **no cron at all** | manual-only since Jul 29–31 |
| 5 | `person` has no `x-lobu-resolution` rules, so dedupe unions nothing | `policy.ts:73-78`, `discovery.ts:100` |
| 6 | Behaviors page reads `last_fired_at`, not `last_run_completed_at` | wrong on 4/4 Behaviors |
| 7 | Orphaned approval notifications render dead "Review & approve" buttons | 8 of 12 have a broken join chain |

Two structural lessons drive the sequencing below. **A DB-only Behavior fix is not durable** —
cause 1 was fixed once and copied back from the stale config. And **`completed` is not a
success signal** — causes 1, 2 and 3 all produced clean-looking completed runs.

Already done this session (not re-planned here): handle fixed in PR #2568 + prod version 7;
Gmail/Spotify/Reminders revived (98 events) and given crons; Behavior 5 now generating tasks;
Behavior 20 walked forward to the current week; CLI context restored to `prod`.

### Decisions taken without sign-off (user was away — reverse any of these freely)

- **P2.1 / P2.2**: fix the `lobu apply` erasure bug *before* configuring any dedupe rules.
- **P2.3**: restore `authored_archive` **and** reconcile the repo config's entity→event drift.
- **P0.2**: capture after-only UI proof; do **not** deliberately re-break a working prod app.
- **P0.2**: de-latch retries forever at a 30-min cap (not "give up after 50 min") — the bug
  being fixed *is* a permanent latch, so a bounded ladder that ends in a latch is a half-fix.
- **P0.2**: workspace-drift **reports**, never blocks — `activeOrg` is unset on some contexts
  and blocking there is the one path that could brick a healthy worker.

**P1.1 is BLOCKED**: it adds a field to the behaviors list API. AGENTS.md requires explicit
sign-off. Do not start it without a yes.

---

## P0 — Unblock and restore collection

### P0.1 Clear the merge queue
`check-drift` fails on **every** open PR: `owletto/main` has `3da851cf` (owletto#741) merged
past the pinned SHA with no parent bump. Not caused by any current work.

The P0.2 pointer bump should subsume this — verify it does, and only open a standalone bump PR
if it doesn't. Then merge **#2568** (green: pre-pr clean, review 0 bugs / 0 blockers, unit +
migrations + format-lint pass).

### P0.2 Mac worker auth — restores 5 connectors
Worktree `.claude/worktrees/mac-context-auth` exists; teammate's design is at
`~/.claude/plans/tranquil-swinging-book-agent-ae4f0b2adb8c16c08.md`.

Root cause is sharper than first diagnosed: `lobu whoami --json` returns
`workerToken = creds.localWorkerToken ?? token` (`packages/cli/src/internal/credentials.ts:120`)
and `LobuCLI.mapWhoami` **prefers `workerToken`**. So the app sent a `/api/local-init` device
PAT — mintable only against loopback — to `https://app.lobu.ai`. Not a stale token; a token
from the wrong universe, knowable before a single request.

Two guards, both driven by a dependency-free `LobuContextIdentity.swift` (reads config.json +
credentials.json, no network):
1. **Pre-flight block** — refuse to send a credential that cannot possibly work.
2. **De-latch** — `credentialsInvalid` must stop being terminal
   (`AppState.swift:~1590` `stopAutoPoll()`). Exit condition: the on-disk identity changes.

`make pre-pr` does **not** run the Swift suite — `apps/mac/Tests/run-tests.sh` is a separate
mandatory gate, run whole (a new dependency breaks every test whose header compiles that file).

E2E is non-negotiable here and runs on the affected machine: RED is `feeds.trigger(309)` →
`worker_claim_timeout` (reproduced live, run 873309). GREEN needs **both** fresh
`[worker] executing whatsapp.local` lines in `~/Library/Logs/Owletto/owletto.log` *and* a 309
trigger that completes. `make owletto-mac INSTALL=1` replaces the running production app — say
so plainly and leave it running.

**Only the user can do**: re-consent Google Calendar (403 `ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT`,
feed 442) and sign in to Revolut in the paired Chrome (16 consecutive failures).

---

## P1 — Make failure visible

Both items here are about the same thing: the system currently renders confident, wrong state.

### P1.1 Behaviors page "last run"  ⚠️ BLOCKED ON SIGN-OFF
`manage_behaviors/list.ts:57` selects `i.last_fired_at` and never selects
`last_run_completed_at`. `behaviors-page.tsx:196` renders it; `:97` falls through to
`"Never run"` on null. `last_fired_at` is only stamped by *event-trigger* activations, so every
schedule-only Behavior reads as never-run. The sidebar is already correct —
`agent-thread-list.ts:283` reads the right column, and `table-schema.ts:494` documents it as
"what the listing orders by". The list already **sorts** by it and **labels** with the other one.

Add `i.last_run_completed_at` to the projection, to `BehaviorRecord`
(`packages/owletto/src/lib/api/behaviors.ts`), and prefer it in `LastRunChip` with
`last_fired_at` as fallback. Additive; nothing removed.

Verify against the four known-wrong rows (5, 20, 70, 71) — all four must flip from
"19 days / 1 day / absent / Never run" to their true `last_run_completed_at`.

### P1.2 Orphaned approvals
There is **no notifications table** (dropped by `20260513200000_notifications_as_events.sql`).
State is three tables chained only at read time — `notifications/service.ts:556-609`:
`notification event.metadata.resource_id` → proposal `events` row → `runs`. Both are
`LEFT JOIN`s **with no filter that drops the notification when the chain breaks**, so an orphan
returns with `approval_status` NULL, falls through `attention-inbox.tsx:680-700` to the generic
CTA, and survives the `:382` filter on the `item.unread` leg alone. The href is a string
persisted at send time, so it always looks valid. Clicking it silently renders an empty page.

Three fixes, smallest first:
1. **Read path** (the user-visible one): in `activity-feed.ts:363-429` / `attention-inbox.tsx`,
   distinguish "approval chain broken" from "plain notification" and stop emitting an
   actionable CTA. The code already handles *decided* approvals correctly — it's the
   *vanished* case that falls through.
2. **Stop minting new orphans**: `manage_connections/handlers/crud.ts:2027-2081` cancels
   pending runs only via `feed_id IN (SELECT ... WHERE connection_id = ...)`, but approval runs
   carry `connection_id` with `feed_id IS NULL`. That is exactly how connection 397's
   soft-delete on 2026-08-05 orphaned these 8.
3. **Stop the reaper eating them**: `check-stalled-executions.ts:391-399` hard-DELETEs runs
   older than 30 days with **no `run_type` filter**, and `events_run_id_fkey` is
   `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so it detaches proposal events.

Reuse `expire-pending-approvals.ts` as the shape for any sweep (batched, round-robin across
orgs, re-asserts its predicate in the UPDATE for multi-replica safety). Note
`supersedeActionEvent` looks the proposal up **by `run_id`**, so it is a no-op once `run_id` is
already NULL — it cannot repair an existing orphan.

Must keep green: `integration/notifications/approval-live-state.test.ts`,
`scheduled/__tests__/expire-pending-approvals.test.ts`,

1. snapshot `canvas_windows` — window state decides whether a trigger does anything;
2. trigger, poll to terminal status;

## The bug

`lobu apply` silently destroys parts of an entity type's `metadata_schema` that it cannot express.

`packages/cli/src/commands/_lib/apply/client.ts:661-665` REBUILDS the schema from scratch:

```ts
payload.metadata_schema = { type: "object", properties: properties ?? {}, ...(required ? {required} : {}) };
```

and reads back only `properties`/`required` (`client.ts:256-262`). Any other top-level key on the stored schema is dropped on the next apply, with no warning and no diff.

The key that matters today is `x-lobu-resolution` — the entity-resolution rules read by `packages/server/src/entity-resolution/policy.ts:148-199` (`readEntityResolutionRules`), which decide whether duplicate entities can be auto-merged. So configuring dedupe rules for the `person` type is impossible to make durable until this is fixed: the next `lobu apply` wipes them.

Server side is NOT lossy — the contract accepts arbitrary keys (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity-schema.ts:85-89`, `Type.Record(Type.String(), Type.Unknown())`) and the handler stores what it is sent verbatim (`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity_schema.ts:472-475` — "metadata_schema is stored as the author sent it"; update path at `:586-609`). **The CLI is the only lossy hop.**

The correct behaviour is: when applying, preserve top-level keys that already exist on the live `metadata_schema` and that the config has no way to express. `properties`/`required`/`type` remain config-owned; everything else is carried forward.

Here's your link — it expires in about 90 minutes (2026-08-07 01:43 UTC):

**https://app.lobu.ai/connect/REDACTED/oauth/start**

## But set your expectations — this may not fix it

I checked before generating it, and the simple story doesn't hold:

- `connections.test` says **"Credentials valid"**, `has_token: true`, `has_refresh: true`, not expired.
- Profile 91 `google-calendar-account` already lists `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly` in **both** `requested_scopes` and `granted_scopes`.

So Google is returning `ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT` for `calendar.v3.Events.List` on a token that *has* the calendar scope. That's not a consent problem.

The likeliest real cause: connection 418 has `app_auth_profile_id = 21`, which is **`google-gmail-google-app`** — an OAuth app registered under `connector_key: google.gmail`, not `google.calendar`. The calendar connection is minting its tokens through the **Gmail** OAuth client. If that Google Cloud project doesn't have the Calendar API enabled, you get exactly this error no matter what scopes the consent screen grants.

Re-consenting is still the right first move — it's cheap, it mints a fresh token, and it rules out a stale-grant explanation. But if the feed still 403s afterwards, don't re-consent again; the fix is either enabling the Calendar API on that Google Cloud project, or pointing connection 418 at a calendar-specific OAuth app rather than the Gmail one.

Once you've clicked through, tell me and I'll trigger feed 442 and check whether it actually pulls events — not just whether the connection reports healthy, since it already does.

## Confidence

- **Link is valid and correctly scoped to connection 418 — 95.** Returned by `connections.reauthenticate` against that connection id, auth profile `google-calendar-account`.
- **That re-consent alone fixes the 403 — 35.** The scope is already granted and the token already valid, which is most of the reason I doubt it.
- **App/profile mismatch is the cause — 60.** The `google.gmail` app on a `google.calendar` connection is real and I read it straight from the row, but I haven't confirmed which APIs are enabled on that Google Cloud project — I can't see that from here, and you can.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

The session began as an audit of the `buremba` prod org and evolved into a systematic repair effort. The user's requests, in order:

1. **Audit**: "check buremba org and all data, tell me if everything looks good and everything is building beatifgully. i want to see approval flows, some recent conversations in the sidebar from that user"
2. **Make things work**: "i want all of them to work and generate things and be actually useful"
3. **Clarify**: "what's bu7emba?"
4. **Iterate operationally**: "can you actually iterate on the data being collected, produce some windows and let's make all of them working one by one. ah yes my twitter is bu7emba and mac mini timelie etc all needs to be connecting"
5. **Challenge a wrong diagnosis**: "it's already autheed no, is there a bug?"
6. **Delegate + teach**: "you can fix it properly test e2e and make sure it works. but launch a teammate to do it so we don't get distracted here. now how can you test the behaviors end to end"
7. **Plan**: "let's plan all properly" → then "ask again", "do the best nxt actions", "and fix issues"
8. **Current**: "google calendar send me the link so i can login"

The through-line intent: Behaviors report `status: completed` while producing nothing, and nothing surfaces the failure. The user wants them actually generating useful output, wants the Mac/data collection connected, and wants proper fixes (not workarounds) verified end-to-end.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **Lobu Behaviors** run on **windows**; `computePendingWindow` (`packages/server/src/utils/window-utils.ts`) chains off the last window's `window_start` and clamps to the current period. No hourly granularity — an hourly cron gets a DAILY window.
- **`canvas_windows`** table is ground truth for behavior output: `content_analyzed`, `extracted_data`, `run_id`. Errors hide in `extracted_data->'run_metadata'->>'error'`, NOT `runs.error_message`.
- **`lobu apply`** is a declarative config→prod sync that is a *blind overwrite* with no drift detection.
- **Device workers**: Owletto Mac app + Chrome extension; `worker_claim_timeout` means the device is gone, not a connector bug.
- **Notifications are events**: no notifications table (dropped by `20260513200000_notifications_as_events.sql`); state spans `events` + `notification_targets` + `runs`, joined at read time.
- **Entity resolution**: `x-lobu-resolution` rules on `entity_types.metadata_schema`; `discovery.ts` unions candidates only on identical normalized keys.
- **Evals program** (#2564): `runs.outcome` taxonomy (PR 1 merged as #2566, squash `b0198396`), capture mode (PR 2, unbuilt).
- MCP tools: `query_sql` (table allowlist), `query_sdk` (read), `run_sdk` (write), `search_sdk`.
- Gates: `make pre-pr`, `make review-fix`, `make review`, `make ui-review`, `make task-setup NAME=<slug>`.

## 3. Files and Code Sections

```
→ lower(coalesce(metadata->>'author_handle','')) = 'bu7emba'
```
Red: 0 rows. Green: 12 rows. `bu7emba` has 24 tweets in 21 days; `buremba` never appeared as an author_handle. Also relevant: `client.ts:661-665` rebuild erases `x-lobu-resolution`.

## 4. Errors and Fixes

- **Wrong initial diagnosis ("re-authenticate the Owletto app")**. User pushed back: "it's already autheed no, is there a bug?" I re-investigated per the standing instruction and found the real cause (ambient global CLI context / loopback PAT sent to prod). I acknowledged the error plainly.
- **`log` shadowed by a zsh function** — my `log show ... 2>/dev/null` returned 0 lines, which I nearly read as "no logs". My own memory `reference_mac_app_logging_and_log_shadowing.md` documented this exact trap. Fixed by reading `~/Library/Logs/Owletto/owletto.log` directly.
- **Piped `make` exit code false green** — `make review 2>&1 | tail` exited 0 while the reviewer had FAILED. Grepped for the verdict marker instead; the codex reviewer is known-broken → `REVIEWER_CLI=claude make review` (verdict: bug_free 88, simplicity 100, 0 bugs, 0 blockers).
- **`query_sql` table allowlist** — `information_schema`, `device_workers`, `runs`, `watchers` are not queryable; used `query_sdk` → `client.query` instead.
- **`OutputSizeExceeded` in `query_sdk`** — the SDK call trace records full intermediate results, so multi-call read scripts blow the 1MB cap even when returning a tiny value. Fixed by narrowing filters.
- **Prod 503 outage mid-session** — `/api/health` returned 503 on all attempts; `kubectl` showed the deployment scaled to 0. Diagnosed as a Flux HelmRelease upgrade doing a zero-overlap cutover. Recovered in ~10s on revision `b0198396`.
- **`?needs_attention=1` was a wrong URL guess** — fell back to "All activity"; corrected by clicking the actual tab (`?lens=attention`).
- **Over-claimed Behavior 71 was broken** — corrected: it emits 2–7 signal events every hour; `content_analyzed: 0` is a bookkeeping artifact.

## 5. Problem Solving

**Solved:**
- bu7emba handle bug (PR #2568 + prod version 7 via `behaviors.createVersion`)
- Revived Gmail (40 events), Spotify (50), Reminders (8) — all had NO cron; gave them staggered schedules (`12 */2`, `22 */2`, `32 */3`, `42 8`)
- Behavior 5 now generates — produced 3 real tasks ("Buy peanut butter", "Buy yoghurt", "Register for the 'Coding in Flow' event")
- Behavior 20 walked forward from Jul 19 to the current week (3 triggers)
- Mac auth root cause found; CLI context restored to `prod` (`orgSlug: buremba` confirmed)

**Diagnosed, not yet fixed:**
- Behaviors page last-run (agent running)
- Orphaned approvals (8 of 12; connection 397 soft-deleted 2026-08-05 is the origin)
- Behavior 20 emits nothing (no `x-lobu-resolution` rules; `name_key` not a rule field)
- `lobu apply` erasure (agent running)

# A green `connections.test` says nothing about scopes

Verified 2026-08-07 on connection **418** (`google.calendar`, org `buremba`), feed **442**.

Feed 442 had failed **12 consecutive times** with
`ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT` on `calendar.v3.Events.List`, while:

```
connections.test({connection_id: 418})
  → {"status":"ok","message":"Credentials valid","has_token":true,
     "has_refresh":true,"expires_at":"2026-08-07T00:56:26.943Z"}
```

and `auth_profiles` 91 listed `.../auth/calendar.readonly` in **both**
`requested_scopes` and `granted_scopes`.

**`connections.test` only checks that a token row exists and has not expired.
It does not call the provider.** So it is green during exactly the outage you
are trying to diagnose. `granted_scopes` is likewise a record of what the
consent screen *returned at grant time*, not what the live token still carries.
Neither is evidence. The only real test is triggering the feed.

## I talked myself out of the correct fix

I noticed connection 418 has `auth_profile_id = 91` (`google.calendar`) but
`app_auth_profile_id = 21` = **`google-gmail-google-app`** (`connector_key:
google.gmail`) — the Calendar connection mints tokens through the *Gmail* OAuth
client. That mismatch is **real but benign**: the Google Cloud project behind it
has the Calendar API enabled, and it had been working for weeks. I rated
re-consent at 35% and the mismatch at 60%. Re-consent fixed it immediately.

**Lesson: a structural oddity you just discovered is not more likely to be the
cause than the boring stale-grant explanation, especially when the oddity
predates the failure.** Check *when* the suspicious config was introduced
against when the failures started before promoting it to prime suspect.

## The fix, end to end

```
client.connections.reauthenticate({connection_id: 418})
  → connect_url https://app.lobu.ai/connect/<token>/oauth/start   (~45 min TTL)
```
Hand the URL to Burak — **never drive an OAuth consent screen yourself**
(credentials). After he completed it, `expires_at` moved `00:56` → `01:45`
(proof a fresh token was minted), and `feeds.trigger(442)` gave
`last_sync_status: success`, `consecutive_failures: 12 → 0`, **20 new events**
(254 total).

## …and it still would not have collected on its own

Feed 442 had **`schedule` and `next_run_at` both NULL** — manual-trigger only,
same defect found the same day on the Gmail, Spotify and Reminders feeds. Set
to `52 */2 * * *`. **Whenever you fix a feed's auth, check its cron in the same
pass** — a working credential on an unscheduled feed still collects nothing, and
`last_sync_status: success` will happily describe that state forever. Same
family as [[reference_x_handle_is_bu7emba_not_buremba]] and the
"`completed` is not a success signal" theme in
[[project_behaviors_known_unfixed_2026_08_05]].

## The opencode session

`ses_026e0d1a5ffe…` was in `opencode.db` (SQLite), not the JSON storage tree I searched first — that's why I missed it. Session **"Continue and finish work"**, run in this repo, resuming a Claude session.

It did the **keyed Behavior output identity** work and took it all the way to prod:

Its own diagnosis of why CI "wouldn't dispatch" is worth keeping: not the GitHub incident, but a **merge conflict** against `bb2dcba0` (#2559) on the same `persist-behavior-event-output.ts`. A conflicting PR can't build a merge ref, so CI silently never fires. That's a failure mode that looks exactly like an outage.

Two other peer PRs landed alongside it: `ac5570c47` (#2565, *resolve unreviewable pending approvals as expired* — that's my P1.2 orphaned-approvals item, partly addressed by someone else) and `e7c5b11d9` (#2567).

## Two of my four agents finished

**#2570 — `lobu apply` schema erasure.** The real fix, not the allowlist patch:

```
 apply/client.ts     | 57 ++++++-
 apply/apply-cmd.ts  |  9 +-
 + 184 lines of tests across 2 files
```

It found a bug I hadn't anticipated: the entity-type list endpoint also returns **public types from other orgs**, so its first cut could have let a foreign `person` shadow the owned one — pushing another org's `x-lobu-resolution` in, or erasing yours. Now reads the ownership-filtered row. Review caught it; that's the gate working.

It also audited Behavior versions for the same class and found they're *not* affected — `createBehaviorVersion` is field-granular, not a rebuild, so omitted fields inherit rather than clear. Good news for the ownership problem: only entity schemas were lossy.

**#2571 + owletto#742 — Behaviors last-run.** Server projection + UI chip, mutation-proved red→green, booted before/after on seeded copies of your four real rows.

**My brief to it was wrong on the mechanism** and `review-fix` caught it. `last_fired_at` isn't stamped by event-trigger activations — `watchers.last_fired_at` has exactly three writers, all in `worker-api/run-lifecycle.ts`. The real split is *which terminal writer finishes the run*: the failure path stamps `last_fired_at`, the completion trigger only fires on `status='completed'`. Fix direction unchanged, comments now say the defensible thing.

## Two decisions I need from you

1. **Merge order.** owletto#742 must merge before #2571 can pass `check-drift` and `ui-review` — both are red purely on that. I told the agent not to merge, so it stopped. Want me to merge owletto#742, re-point the parent, and re-run `ui-review` with the artifact?
2. **`order_by: "last_fired_at"`** in the `manage_behaviors` contract still sorts by the stale column while the UI now displays the completion stamp. Nothing diverges visibly today (the page uses default order), but they now disagree. API-surface call, so it's yours.

## Confidence

- **opencode session findings — 94.** Read the session's own text, then independently verified the merge SHA against `origin/main` and the live health endpoint. I did not re-verify its 9-row backfill.
- **#2570 correctness — 78.** Full CLI suite plus two mutation red→greens, but the agent never ran a real `lobu apply` end-to-end — it rated that surface 40 itself and said so.
- **#2571 correctness — 90.** Booted before/after plus mutation test; proof used seeded copies of prod rows, not prod.
- **Prod state of orphaned approvals — 30.** #2565 landed and plausibly covers it, but I haven't re-checked the 8 orphans.

## Next actions

1. Say go and I'll merge owletto#742 → re-point #2571 → clear both red checks.
2. Re-check the 8 orphaned approvals now that #2565 is live — cheap, and it may close P1.2 outright.
3. After #2570 ships, re-stamp `x-lobu-resolution` on `buremba`'s `person` type — the fix stops future erasure but doesn't restore what's already gone, which still blocks the dedupe work.

Of the 254 google.calendar rows, **213 are future-dated, 203 beyond +1 year, latest

in the other direction, because a task/assistant Behavior wants *upcoming* meetings.
**Calendar needs its own bounded source** (`BETWEEN now() - 1 day AND now() + 7 days`,
`ORDER BY occurred_at ASC`), separate from the past-facing signal source. A single
shared `LIMIT` is one budget that any high-volume kind can monopolise.

Generalises beyond calendar: `occurred_at` is the *event's* time, not ingest time. Any
connector emitting future-dated rows (calendar, reminders, scheduled posts) silently
dominates a recency-ordered window. Sort by `created_at` or bound the window per kind.

at deploy — so fixing the connector source covers the DB row; no hand DB edit needed.

real exception to [[feedback_never_mirror_an_encoding_in_sql]] — verify reachability
before assuming a resync backfill will work.
